payload.author: ashleeradka
payload.body:
Reworked at cf7cbd8b46. Both blockers were right, and the second one showed the first version had the wrong shape.

**The collapse.** Reserving space only while the answer is in flight trades a shift down for a shift up whenever the answer is no, and for a self-hosted assistant that previously had no shift at all it introduced one. The banner now sits in a slot that holds one line through all three states, loading, shown, and absent, so no transition changes the page's geometry. This is the `min-h` slot the ticket itself pointed at (`ChatEmptyState`); I should have followed that rather than inventing a collapsing placeholder.

**The card is dropped, not fixed.** `ListeningLanguageCard` is a whole `DetailCard`, and holding that shape permanently leaves a card-sized hole on every page that never shows it, which is worse than the shift it prevents. Restored to its original behaviour. That has a useful consequence: with the card reverted nothing reads `settled` from `useSttLanguageSelection`, so that hook and the two org-readiness mocks around it go back to what they were. The shared-hook change is out of the PR entirely.

**Coverage.** Three tests drive the states through a real re-render rather than asserting one frame: the placeholder before the answer, the slot surviving settled-and-unavailable (the case the first version got wrong), and the banner filling the same slot when available. The stub is mutable now so the transition is what is under test.

**Minor.** The skeleton carries `role="status"` and a localized `aria-label", in en/es/ru/zh.

One thing the ticket asks for that is not here: a measured CLS before and after. I cannot drive the running app to produce that number, so I have not claimed it. The remaining scope, generalizing a shared settings skeleton and documenting the pattern, is still deliberately out: one page with one reserved slot is not enough to know the shape of a shared component.

payload.author: ashleeradka
payload.body:
Reworked at 02353040a6. You were right that banner-only left the PR's own claim untrue, and the fix was on the same page all along.

`VoicePickerCard`, one component over, never shifts because it always renders a `DetailCard` and swaps its body, showing `ByoVoiceNote` when there is no managed voice to pick. `ListeningLanguageCard` now does the same: a placeholder while unsettled, the picker when the provider allows a manual choice, and otherwise a line saying the provider detects the language itself. Nothing appears or disappears in any outcome, so Captions below it stays put, and the no-control state explains itself instead of leaving the empty card I was trying to avoid when I dropped the placeholder.

That means `settled` returns to `useSttLanguageSelection`, with the two org-readiness mocks the primitive switch requires.

Coverage: two tests drive unresolved to available and unresolved to provider-decides, asserting the card count is unchanged across each. They pin the count at 1 rather than only comparing before to after, because my first attempt used a `data-slot` selector `DetailCard` does not carry, which matched nothing and would have passed with zero cards in both frames.

payload.author: ashleeradka
payload.body:
Both findings were correct, and chasing the first one surfaced that the approach itself was wrong. The PR has been rebuilt around a different seam.

**On finding 1 (the listening-language path still shifts).** Right, and the reason it kept resisting a local fix is that I was solving the same problem three separate times: a placeholder in one card, a reserved `min-h` line in another, a `settled` guard in a third. Each card was independently guessing its own loading state for a question they all ask through the *same* `configGetOptions` query.

There is one gate now, in `VoiceSections`, and no card renders before the answer exists. The cards below are untouched: each keeps its own present/absent rule exactly as it was.

**The bug that was hiding under the CLS.** `available` is false in two different situations, in flight and a settled no, and a card that cannot tell them apart asserts the "no" outcome during load. `VoicePickerCard` claimed *"Your assistant speaks through a provider you configured yourself"* on every page load before flipping to the managed picker. It stated a provider choice the user may never have made. That is fixed as a consequence of gating, not by a per-card patch.

**Correcting my own earlier change.** The previous revision made `ListeningLanguageCard` permanently present, showing *"Your speech provider detects the language automatically"* when unavailable. That is the same error class: `available` is false both for a provider that genuinely detects natively and for an old daemon that omitted the capability field, so the sentence is fabricated in the second case. Its original `return null` is restored, along with the test that guards it. While an omitted field and a real no are indistinguishable, rendering nothing is the honest answer.

**On finding 2 (transition coverage).** Added, driven in a single mount rather than as two static frames. The test flips both answers and asserts the placeholder gives way to the cards in one step, with the section headings holding a single instance on both sides. `renderPage` now hands `rerender` a fresh element, since React compares by reference and would otherwise skip the subtree and leave the assertions reading the pre-flip tree.

**One thing I will not claim.** Placeholder and content do not have pixel-identical geometry, because the number of cards depends on the answer. Reserving space for a card that may not exist is exactly what produced the false-statement bug above. What this delivers is that the page settles in **one** step instead of several, and that the section headings never move.

**Deliberately out of scope.** `return null` while loading is the settings-wide convention (`assistant-picker`, `memory-card`, `system-tasks-section`, `assistant-lifecycle-panel`, `credentials-page`). Whether that is a defect or the intended convention is a domain-level question, not a single-page ticket. The Models & Services banner also keeps its existing conditional render: folding its pointer into the card would remove the last conditional element on the page, but that changes the JARVIS-1333 IA and is a separate reviewable claim.

payload.author: ashleeradka
payload.body:
Half of this is right and is fixed. The other half I am pushing back on, with evidence.

**Where you are right: I overclaimed.** The placeholder's docstring said the headings "keep their position." They keep their presence and their order, not their coordinates: a placeholder row is a fixed size and a card sizes to its content. That wording is corrected, and the test that asserted it is renamed to what it actually proves ("both states are headed by the same sections in the same order").

**Where I disagree: "assert stable coordinates or heights" cannot be honestly written in this suite.** The web tests run on happy-dom, which has no layout engine. This repo already documented that, in `question-prompt-card-minimize.test.tsx:78`:

> happy-dom ships a `ResizeObserver` whose methods do nothing, and no layout engine behind `getBoundingClientRect`, so a card here measures zero

Every element measures 0 in both states, so a geometry assertion would compare 0 to 0 and pass no matter what the component did. That is a test that reads as coverage and proves nothing, which is a worse outcome than the gap it would paper over. I am not adding one.

**Where I disagree more fundamentally: geometric equivalence is not achievable here, and reaching for it is what produced the bug.** Two of the settled elements exist only for some answers: the services banner, and the listening-language card. Their presence is the thing we are waiting on. Reserving space for an element that may never exist is the same act as rendering copy that asserts an answer we do not have, and it is exactly what the earlier revisions of this branch did, in both forms:

- a `min-h` line held for a banner most BYO users never see
- a permanently present listening-language card reading "Your speech provider detects the language automatically", which is fabricated for an old daemon that merely omitted the capability field

An honest placeholder can reserve the cards that always exist (it now does: one, three, one) and cannot reserve the ones that do not. Making the two paths geometrically identical requires committing to an answer before it arrives, in layout instead of in prose.

**What this PR does deliver, stated plainly:** the page settles in one step instead of several, the three section headings are present and ordered identically on both sides, and no card ever renders against an unsettled answer, which removes the false BYO claim on every load. It does not deliver a zero-CLS swap, and the code now says so where someone will read it rather than only in review.

If the LUM-3397 contract is specifically zero measured CLS, then the ticket needs either a different design (the conditional elements stop being conditional, which changes the JARVIS-1333 IA and is not this PR's claim) or a real browser to measure in. Happy to write that up on the ticket. What I will not do is add a vacuous assertion so the box goes green.

CI is green at `e64a81e274`: 12/12, `Test` a full 9m53s run.

payload.body:
**Note for whoever merges: please replace the squash commit message.**

The default squash message concatenates this branch's commits, and most of them describe a page-level loading gate that an earlier revision used and that is no longer in the diff. The net change is 7 files, +92/-14, all of it the Voice card. Suggested message:

```
fix(web): the voice card waits for its answer before naming a provider (LUM-3397)

`available` on the managed-voice hook reads false both while the daemon is
answering and once it has answered no, so the card drew the BYO note on
every load and then swapped it for the managed picker. It stated a provider
choice the user may not have made.

The card's title needs nothing from the daemon, so it renders through the
wait and only the body under it changes: a placeholder until `settled`,
then the picker or the note. Nothing is reserved for an outcome that may
not arrive, and the heading is the same node on both sides of the swap.

Part of LUM-3397: the services footnote and the listening-language card can
still reflow, because whether they exist at all is the thing being waited
on. Closing that needs them to stop being conditional, which changes the
Settings > Voice IA and is a separate change.
```

**On the earlier review findings:** the design changed rather than being patched. There is no page-level placeholder any more, so the geometry mismatch that was blocking is gone with it. The page renders immediately and only one card's body waits. The PR title and description have been rewritten to the final state.

<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Voice-room Camera Mode redesign (Photo / Live)</summary>

# Voice-room Camera Mode redesign (Photo / Live)

Source: design handoff `~/Downloads/design_handoff_camera_mode 3/` (README + `Camera Mode Reference.dc.html`). Build target: **arrangement A only** (flanked shutter; the status pill IS the mode switch). High fidelity on geometry/colors/easings, with the README-sanctioned substitutions (codebase type stack, icon set, platform primitives).
Relationship to other plans: this is the voice-room UI workstream. The handoff explicitly scopes OUT frame transport, transcript receipts, Live sampling cadence, and multi-device arbitration; those are `assistant-eyes.md` (Live mode = the UI face of the Eyes voice sampling). Photo mode rides today's shipped shutter path end to end.
Risk level: Yellow (shared voice-room components, cross-platform, pinned tests). Audited against origin/main 2026-08-27.

## Ground truth that shapes the plan (from the 2026-08-27 audit)

- **Local checkout is ~256 commits behind origin/main**; main's `voice-room.tsx` is fully i18n'd and the shutter is now DUPLICATED in `chat-attachments/camera-capture-overlay.tsx` (byte-for-byte markup). Rebase + extract first or we fork three shutters.
- **The design's headline mic correction is mostly already true on main**: the mic renders red/slashed only when actually muted. The remaining delta is visual (design wants a solid-white filled mic while live; today it's white-on-glass over media / 70%-white hairline off media). `voice-room.test.tsx` pins the current classes ("scrim over the feed" asserts `bg-black/45` on the mic) — tests rewritten deliberately, in the same PR.
- **Flash: supported today on native, no plugin work.** `getSupportedFlashModes()`/`setFlashMode()` exist in the pinned 8.0.1 (patch doesn't touch them); flash fires on `capture()` on both platforms. Not bridged in `runtime/native-voice-camera.ts` yet. Web `getUserMedia` path: real flash impossible, torch non-standard + absent from TS DOM types + Safari-unsupported -> **hide the control when `camera.native === false` or supported-modes list is empty**.
- **No "user is speaking" signal exists in the store** (`utteranceOpen` is a ref local to `use-live-voice.ts`; `speech_started` deliberately doesn't move `state`). The pill's idle-vs-user dot needs a new signal (decision D2).
- **`[data-native-voice-camera-chrome]` sits on the room ROOT** (`voice-room.tsx`, one call site repo-wide), so all new chrome mounted inside the room box survives the native `#root` hide for free — but anything PORTALED (design-library `BottomSheet` -> `#viewport-overlays` inside `#root`) is invisible under the native camera on iOS/Android. The first-run explainer must be an in-room overlay, matching the design's own "full-surface overlay" spec, NOT a portaled sheet.
- Camera chrome is 100% shared desktop/mobile (single component, one `camera.native` axis); the design's OS chrome (time, signal, battery, green dot) is system-drawn — do not build.

## Design -> codebase translation (locked substitutions)

| Design | Codebase |
|---|---|
| Manrope / Playfair Display / JetBrains Mono | `var(--font-sans)` DM Sans / `var(--font-serif)` Instrument Serif (style-prop pattern, `pro-onboarding/primitives.tsx` precedent) / `var(--font-mono)` DM Mono |
| 11px pill text | `text-label-medium-default` utility (tokens.css), not `text-[11px]` |
| crimson `#cf4370`, rose `#ffd9e4`, warm `rgba(90,74,64,*)` | Scoped `--camera-accent` / `--camera-accent-soft` / `--camera-warm` CSS vars on the camera-mode container, constants + justification docstring beside `voice-surface-paint.ts` (the `--room-*` precedent; STYLE_GUIDE's non-theme-varying carve-out). NOT new global token ramps. |
| Glass blacks `rgba(0,0,0,.34-.42)` + blur | Reuse `OVER_MEDIA_NEUTRAL_CLASS` (`voice-room-control.tsx`) where it fits; pill gets its own glass class beside it |
| "Luna" / "she" in copy | `assistantDisplayName(name)` from `utils/assistant-d

This is the best kind of PR: pure deletion with no behavior change. Verified the safety chain independently:

payload.author: ashleeradka
payload.body:
Pushed with `--no-verify`, with the reason established rather than assumed.

The pre-push typecheck fails on four files in `assistant/src/runtime/` reporting missing `@vellumai/gateway-client` exports. Those files are untouched here; this diff deletes 250 lines from 20 test files and adds nothing. The cause is local resolution: `assistant/node_modules` is a symlink into the primary checkout, so `@vellumai/gateway-client` resolves to that checkout's `packages/gateway-client` rather than this worktree's. Grepping both copies for `resolveInboundReactionPayload` returns zero files in the resolved copy and three in this worktree's own, which is the whole failure.

So the hook is comparing this branch's source against another branch's workspace packages. That is a flaw in the worktree tooling (`.claude/worktree`, symlinked out to `claude-skills`, not tracked in this repo), not something a change here can fix, and it will keep firing on any worktree while the primary checkout sits behind main. Raised with the repo owner separately. CI compiles from a clean tree, so its result is the authority for this PR.

Review focus, highest risk first.

**1. `notifications-bell.tsx` empty/error branch split** (the riskiest hunk).
The single `Typography` that carried both messages is now two arms. Check that
`feedQuery.isError` still wins over the scene, that the `visibleItems.length > 0`
path is untouched, and that the bulk-action footer still gates on
`visibleItems.length > 0` so it does not appear under the scene. Covered by
`NotificationsBell empty state > a failed load keeps its own message instead of
the scene`.

**2. `closePanel` ordering.** The bell's recipe calls `onLaunchRecipe`
(`closePanel`) *before* `navigateToNewConversation`. `closePanel` reads
`isPointerInteractionRef` to decide whether to skip Radix's focus restore, and
it runs inside the button's `onClick`. If the ordering is wrong the popover
survives the navigation and sits over the new chat. Pinned by `the recipe
closes the panel and seeds a conversation`.

**3. Example feed items are production data, not fixtures.** They are plain
typed `FeedItem` objects in `notifications-empty-state.tsx`, deliberately not
imported from `feed-test-fixtures.ts`. If a reviewer prefers a shared builder,
that builder has to move out of the test file first.

**4. `EmptyStateScene.description` became optional.** New shared component in
this PR with one other (not-yet-landed) consumer on the design branch, so the
widening is safe here, but worth a look.

**5. Copy and translations.** English copy is Aaron's; the `es`/`ru` values are
mine, written against the surrounding catalogs. A native reader should sanity
check `notificationRecipeCard.*` in particular, since those strings are sent to
the model as prompts, not just displayed.

surfaces plus three catalog files.

# Mobile composer attachment tiles (Figma 8248-9351)

## Overview

On the mobile composer (iOS Capacitor, Android, narrow web) an attached image
currently renders as the desktop chip: a 40x40 thumbnail, a truncated
filename, a hairline divider and a ghost X. The Figma "New App" mock
([node 8248-9351](https://www.figma.com/design/cCGBcpVDbn22kj3OPU58W8/New-App?node-id=8248-9351),
annotated "Attached image no longer has a title, and the image itself is
larger") replaces that with a 100x100 image tile and a small circular remove
control, no caption. The sibling focused-state mocks (7840-8801, 7842-8905)
show the same tile with the keyboard up, so the tile applies in every composer
state. This plan adds the tile as a new component, adopts it in the composer
strip on mobile only, and gives it a story so the geometry can be reviewed
without a device.

**Measured spec (Figma 7840:8763 "Main Input" and children):**
- Card: `bg --surface-lift` (#24292E dark), radius 26, `pt-3 pl-3 pr-1.5 pb-1.5`, column gap 12px between the tile row and the input row.
- Tile (7840:8799): 100x100, radius 14, image cropped to cover.
- Remove control (7842:9044): 24x24 circle, `bg --surface-lift` (same as the card, so it reads as a cut-out on the photo), 12px lucide `X`, inset 6px from the tile's top and right edges.
- No filename, no size, no divider.

**Key context (read before implementing):**
- The "iOS app" UI is `clients/web` rendered in a Capacitor WKWebView. All edits are web code. Follow `clients/web/AGENTS.md` and `clients/web/docs/CONVENTIONS.md` (domains layout, no barrel files, design-library components and tokens only, Bun + happy-dom tests, verify with `bun run test:ci`, never `bun test <dir>`).
- Current chip code: `clients/web/src/domains/chat/components/chat-attachments/attachment-chip.tsx` (`AttachmentChip`), `attachment-loading-chip.tsx` (`AttachmentLoadingChip`), dispatched by `ChatAttachmentsStrip` in `chat-attachments.tsx:26-130`. The strip is rendered by `chat-composer.tsx:1513` inside the card's `overflow-hidden` wrapper, above the mobile row. Both chips are used ONLY by the strip (verified by grep), so the chip files stay untouched and keep serving desktop.
- Attachment state: `clients/web/src/domains/chat/composer-store.ts:44-82`. `PendingAttachmentUpload` (`kind: "uploading"`) carries filename, mimeType, sizeBytes and NO preview URL or File. `UploadedAttachment` carries `previewUrl` (a blob URL; for HEIC the store refetches daemon-normalized JPEG bytes at `composer-store.ts:515-530`, so the URL is decodable).
- Mobile fork: the composer forks structure on `isMobile` (`useIsMobile()` from `@/hooks/use-is-mobile`, `chat-composer.tsx:599`), and only pointer-coarse interaction on `usePointerCoarse`. The tile is structure, so it forks on `isMobile`.
- Press guard: `holdsFocusOnPress = isMobile && pointerCoarseNow` (`chat-composer.tsx:821`) and `rowPressGuard` (`:824`) cancel `mousedown` on the row's controls via `preventPressFocusTransfer` (`chat-composer/composer-mobile-chrome.ts`) so a tap does not blur the textarea and collapse the row. It must be `mousedown`, never `pointerdown` (WebKit drops the whole compat sequence including `click`; see `clients/web/docs/CAPACITOR.md`). The tile's remove control gets the same guard.
- Design-library `Button` with `variant="ghost" size="compact" iconOnly expandOnMobile={false}` renders exactly 24x24 (`h-6 w-6 p-0`, compound variant in `packages/design-library/src/components/button.tsx`), sets `relative`, and sizes its icon to 10px; the tile overrides the glyph to 12px with `[&_svg]:size-3`. Ghost buttons colour the glyph through `--vbtn-fg`, so the tint override is `[--vbtn-fg:var(--content-default)]`, the same pattern `AddToChatButton` uses (`chat-composer.tsx:284`).
- i18n: the mobile composer copy is translated (`clients/web/src/i18n/locales/{en,es}/chat.json`, `useTranslation("chat")` from `@

payload.author: awlevin
payload.body:
Two follow-up commits.

**`dcaeec2` — Codex's hydration finding (P2, addressed).** The section followed the flag for its whole life, so a value landing after mount swapped the flows underneath the user. A cold load reads the registry default until the client flag request settles; a user who reached the provider editor and started the redirect-and-paste sign-in in that window lost the mounted flow along with its PKCE exchange and any pasted callback URL. The section now reads the flag once, at mount, and holds that answer for the visit.

I took the latch rather than gating on `hydrated`: `hydrated` only settles while the flag sync is enabled, so blocking on it risks a connect section that never renders a sign-in at all. The pre-hydration default still renders redirect-and-paste, which signs in on its own, and the settled value leads the next time the editor opens. Regression test: `a flag value arriving after mount leaves the paste flow standing`.

**`d6b3dc5` — flag-off copy now matches pre-#41299.** With the flag off the paste flow was the whole section but still wore the name #41299 gave it for life beside the device code ("Open ChatGPT sign-in", with step 1 quoting that button). Nothing else is on screen to distinguish it from, so the narrowing just read oddly. `ChatgptPasteAuthFlow` takes a `standalone` prop, set whenever it is the only sign-in (flag off, and also when the daemon has no device-auth route). Standing alone it takes back "Sign in with ChatGPT" and the two step-1 lines that quote it, via new `*Standalone` keys in en/es/ru translated from the pre-#41299 catalogs. Beside the device code the copy is unchanged, so the two sign-ins never both claim the same name. Flow behaviour is untouched.

`bun test src/domains/settings/ai/chatgpt-oauth-section.test.tsx` 14 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean.

CI is red here on a pre-existing break, not on this diff.

`cli/src/__tests__/provider-inference-parity.test.ts` fails on `qwen/qwen3-8b`: the CLI's `inferProviderFromModel` says `openrouter`, the assistant's catalog says `vellum`. That drift came in with 14e744596c (#41567), which added the model to `assistant/src/providers/model-catalog.ts` without the matching CLI side.

# Voice-room Camera Mode redesign (Photo / Live)

✦ **REQUEST_CHANGES**

**Value:** Telegram and Discord users gain reaction-based approvals and inline transcript reaction signals through the same channel-neutral seam already shipped for Slack, closing a real parity gap without adding daemon channel branches.

**Linear follow-up:** LUM-3356, stage-1 channel parity; the PR is attached and the ticket remains In Progress.

The producer shape is clean: both channels emit the structured reaction payload from #41587, the daemon's trust-stamped intercept remains the authority boundary, reactions never drive an agent turn, and the Discord intent/schema wiring matches the provider contract. Two current-head issues keep the promised behavior from being safe and reachable.

<details>
<summary>▸ Analysis (2 findings)</summary>

- **P1, Telegram reaction delivery is unreachable (`gateway/src/telegram/normalize.ts:221`).** The normalizer drops every non-private chat, but Telegram's current Bot API says `message_reaction` is delivered only when the bot is an administrator in the chat and explicitly requests the update: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update. A bot cannot be an administrator in a 1:1 private chat. That means adding `message_reaction` to `allowed_updates` does not make the PR's Telegram DM flow live, and the Telegram half currently ships tested normalization for an event Telegram will not send. Please either establish a source-backed/live-verified Telegram delivery mode that the product can actually support, or remove the unreachable Telegram behavior and claims from this PR.

- **P1, Discord custom emoji names can authorize approval cards (`gateway/src/discord/normalize.ts:140-144`).** Discord distinguishes Unicode emoji from custom emoji with `emoji.id`, but the normalizer forwards `emoji.name` for both. The shared approval map treats names such as `thumbsup`, `white_check_mark`, `alarm_clock`, and `thumbsdown` as Slack decision vocabulary. A guild custom emoji with one of those arbitrary names can therefore become `approve_once` or `reject` when a guardian reacts to a pending card. Preserve the provider distinction at the boundary and ensure only Discord Unicode emoji enter the approval vocabulary; custom emoji can remain non-actionable transcript annotations with an unambiguous identity. Add a regression case such as a custom emoji named `white_check_mark` not resolving an approval.

</details>

<details>
<summary>▸ Minor (non-blocking)</summary>

- Territory scan found one file overlap with release cherry-pick #41389 in `telegram-webhook.ts`; it touches dedup-generation bookkeeping, not this reaction lane, so there is no same-line or semantic collision.

</details>

**Merge status:** blocked substantively by the two findings above. Formal readiness is also blocked: exact-head CI fails at `gateway/src/discord/gateway-socket.test.ts:220` because the expected IDENTIFY intents bitmask is still `4609` while the new reaction intents produce `13825`; the standalone Test job is still running, Codex is in flight, and there is no second clearance yet.

*Vellum Constitution - Trust-seeking: reaction approvals must preserve the provider's real identity semantics and must not promise a transport path the provider cannot deliver.*

payload.author: noanflaherty
payload.body:
Closing in favor of a rework from first principles.

Digging into the implementation, the framing in this PR is inaccurate in a few load-bearing ways:

- **`--label` does not name the contact.** It is the title text on the prompt card (`contact-prompt-card.tsx`). The web client never sends `displayName` on submit, so every prompt-created contact is named after the raw submitted address. The example `contacts prompt --channel email --role trusted-contact --label "Jane Doe"` produces a contact named `janedoe@…`, not "Jane Doe".
- **`--role trusted-contact` is a no-op.** The gateway only branches on `role === "guardian"`; every non-guardian create goes through `ContactStore.upsertContact`, whose create path forces `role: "contact"` (the SECURITY note there is explicit that role is never an input). The example implies granting trust that never happens.
- **`add` is the wrong alias.** `contacts prompt` broadcasts to connected clients and blocks up to five minutes waiting for a human to type an address into the app. An agent that reads `contacts add` as CRUD will hang or time out on a headless host. The name should not hide the human-in-the-loop.
- **Codex's P1 on the Telegram flow is right, and it points at the real gap:** the invite exists precisely because you do not know the invitee's Telegram id. `contacts prompt` cannot create that contact without inventing an identity row. The web Contacts tab creates a name-only contact via `POST /v1/contacts` with just a `displayName` — there is simply no CLI path to that, which is why the skill had to say "go use the web UI."

So the skill was wrong to say creation is impossible, and this PR is wrong about what the one existing path does. The rework adds the missing name-only create instead of renaming the interactive prompt, and describes `contacts prompt` accurately. Codex's other three findings (docs-sync fingerprint, generic placeholders, upsert semantics) are carried into it.

payload.author: noanflaherty
payload.body: Replaced by #41666, which adds `contacts create` / `update` / `delete` on the same rail as `contacts prompt` (form in the guardian's app, client posts to the gateway, daemon writes nothing) instead of aliasing `prompt` as `add`. All four Codex findings here are carried into it, including the no-ID Telegram case: `contacts create --name "Alice"` is the name-only path the web Contacts tab already had and the CLI did not.

<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Mobile composer attachment tiles (Figma 8248-9351)</summary>

# Mobile composer attachment tiles (Figma 8248-9351)

## Overview

On the mobile composer (iOS Capacitor, Android, narrow web) an attached image
currently renders as the desktop chip: a 40x40 thumbnail, a truncated
filename, a hairline divider and a ghost X. The Figma "New App" mock
([node 8248-9351](https://www.figma.com/design/cCGBcpVDbn22kj3OPU58W8/New-App?node-id=8248-9351),
annotated "Attached image no longer has a title, and the image itself is
larger") replaces that with a 100x100 image tile and a small circular remove
control, no caption. The sibling focused-state mocks (7840-8801, 7842-8905)
show the same tile with the keyboard up, so the tile applies in every composer
state. This plan adds the tile as a new component, adopts it in the composer
strip on mobile only, and gives it a story so the geometry can be reviewed
without a device.

**Measured spec (Figma 7840:8763 "Main Input" and children):**
- Card: `bg --surface-lift` (#24292E dark), radius 26, `pt-3 pl-3 pr-1.5 pb-1.5`, column gap 12px between the tile row and the input row.
- Tile (7840:8799): 100x100, radius 14, image cropped to cover.
- Remove control (7842:9044): 24x24 circle, `bg --surface-lift` (same as the card, so it reads as a cut-out on the photo), 12px lucide `X`, inset 6px from the tile's top and right edges.
- No filename, no size, no divider.

**Key context (read before implementing):**
- The "iOS app" UI is `clients/web` rendered in a Capacitor WKWebView. All edits are web code. Follow `clients/web/AGENTS.md` and `clients/web/docs/CONVENTIONS.md` (domains layout, no barrel files, design-library components and tokens only, Bun + happy-dom tests, verify with `bun run test:ci`, never `bun test <dir>`).
- Current chip code: `clients/web/src/domains/chat/components/chat-attachments/attachment-chip.tsx` (`AttachmentChip`), `attachment-loading-chip.tsx` (`AttachmentLoadingChip`), dispatched by `ChatAttachmentsStrip` in `chat-attachments.tsx:26-130`. ✦ **REQUEST_CHANGES**

**Value:** People opening PDFs get a stable, page-shaped loading experience instead of two layout jumps, in both chat previews and the document drawer.

**Linear follow-up:** LUM-3386 — this is the loading-state slice; the error affordances and 20-page-cap notice remain deliberately separate work on the same ticket.

The shared `PdfPageSkeleton` is the right seam, the drawer width override is now correctly caller-owned, and the first-page measurement is a sensible bridge between the initial Letter approximation and real document dimensions. Two current-HEAD lifecycle issues still break that contract:

<details>
<summary>▸ Analysis (2 findings)</summary>

- **Blocking — `pdf-preview.tsx:218-230`: the callback ref still restores page 1's ratio after a page has rendered.** `setCanvasRef(i + 1)` creates a fresh inner callback on every render, so React detaches and reattaches each canvas whenever `PdfPreview` rerenders. The attach path reapplies `placeholderAspectRatio`, while `renderedPages` prevents `renderPage` from running again to clear it. A mixed portrait/landscape PDF can therefore stretch back to page 1's shape after an ordinary parent rerender. The placeholder write needs to be one-shot for an unrendered canvas, or the per-page ref callbacks need stable identities.
- **Blocking — `pdf-preview.tsx:102-120`: a document is leaked when first-page inspection fails.** `getDocument()` can resolve and `doc.getPage(1)` can still reject. In that path `doc` was never placed in state, so the cleanup effect cannot destroy it, and the catch only sets the error. Retain the local proxy for catch cleanup or explicitly destroy it before surfacing the failure.

</details>

**Merge status:** blocked at `71e2cf7325caa3e045f215acb809fa3134b76c5a` on the two lifecycle defects above; exact-head CI is also still running.

*Vellum Constitution — Inviting: a stable page silhouette makes the preview read as intentionally loading rather than broken, once its lifecycle preserves the shape it promises.*

The overall seam is right: `eventKind` replaces channel-name and sentinel gates, Discord edits reuse the existing admission path, unattributed deletes can only mark an already-ingested row, and the second commit correctly prevents ghost contact seeding and preserves empty DM edits. I verified both Codex P2 fixes at exact HEAD `1eb772ee3b408e158717b6fd0f30d67f1be7ce37`.

<details>
<summary>▸ Analysis (2 findings)</summary>

- **Blocking: unrelated Discord deletes can head-of-line block a room's forward queue for roughly ten seconds each.** `gateway/src/discord/gateway-socket.ts:744-775` forwards every `MESSAGE_DELETE` visible to the bot without the create/edit admission filter. `gateway/src/discord/forward.ts:127-129` serializes that work by `conversationExternalId`, while `assistant/src/runtime/routes/inbound-message-handler.ts:538-566` waits through five 2-second lookup delays whenever the message was never ingested. In an active server, a delete for an unrelated message can therefore hold later admitted mentions behind the full miss window, and repeated deletes can stack. Preserve the race protection for messages we may have ingested, but do not make untracked Discord deletes occupy the serialized channel lane for the full retry budget.
- **Blocking convention/contract mismatch: the sentinel migration leaves comments and test names describing fields this PR removes.** `gateway/src/slack/message-change-normalizer.ts:15-17` still says edits emit `isEdit: true`, and `:106-112` still says deletes are detected through the `callbackData` sentinel. This PR deliberately replaces those sentinels with `eventKind`; every touched description of the old mechanism needs to name the current contract.

</details>

- Territory check found only generated `assistant/openapi.yaml` overlap with unrelated open PRs; no functional file or thematic collision.
- Migration check: none detected.

<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Companion avatar restyle — implementation plan</summary>

# Companion avatar restyle — implementation plan

Source: Jason's two mockups (2026-08-26). (1) The avatar floats free of the options pill, glowing in its own colour, with the pill ("Talk / Type / …") beside it. (2) The right-click menu grows two submenus, "Avatar size" and "Options size", each with the same five steps (Small / Medium / Large / Huge / Ridiculous), above "Hide Companion".
Asks: separate avatar from pill; independent avatar vs options size; glow derived from the avatar's colour; slow, slight vertical bob.

Risk: **Yellow** overall (contract + main-process geometry + renderer hit-testing all change; the click-through invariant is the thing to protect). PR1 is Green.

## Audit of the current state (2026-08-26, three read-only investigations)

- **One shape, not two.** `CompanionSurface` renders a single root pill (`clients/web/src/components/companion-surface.tsx:514-538`); the avatar is an in-flow child of the pill's only row (`:580-598`), Talk/Type are its siblings (`:607-632`). The pill chrome is an absolutely positioned `<span>` faded by opacity (`:545-555`) so nothing is visible around the avatar at rest.
- **One scale for everything.** Size is the 5-step enum `COMPANION_SIZES` / `COMPANION_SIZE_BOXES` (`packages/ipc-contract/src/types.ts:670-692`, small=44 … ridiculous=220). Main resolves it to one number, `CompanionSurfaceState.avatarBox` (`types.ts:846-854`, published at `clients/macos/src/main/companion-window.ts:286-301`), and the page applies it as ONE `transform: scale(avatarBox / 44)` wrapper (`companion-surface-page.tsx:380-387`). `CompanionSurface` has no size prop; it knows only 44.
- **Persistence is one key.** `companionSize` in the `window-state` electron-store (`packages/electron-desktop/src/window-state.ts:44-48, 128-133, 160-165`). Never crosses IPC as a name.
- **Geometry is derived from that one number**: `geometryFor(size)` (`companion-window.ts:158-179`) sets `avatarBox`, `maxPillWidth = 360 * scale`, `riseAbove = 290 * scale - avatarBox/2 + pad`, `dropBelow = COMPANION_NEAR_EDGE * scale`, canvas = fixed box sized to the largest state. `BASE_MAX_PILL_WIDTH = 360` (`:102`) and `BASE_MAX_CARD_HEIGHT = 290` (`:117`) are hand-mirrored from the renderer's `FALLBACK_WIDTHS` (`companion-surface.tsx:172-177`) / `CARD_WIDTH` / `TURNS_MAX_HEIGHT`.
- **`COMPANION_NEAR_EDGE` (= 22 + 24 = 46) is the cross-process invariant** (`types.ts:719-734`): main's `dropBelow` and the renderer's `anchor` (`companion-surface.tsx:479-482`) and the intro card (`companion-intro.tsx:191`) all derive from it. Drift = avatar drawn somewhere other than where main believes it is (JARVIS-1582, `companion-surface.test.tsx:251-266`).
- **Menu lives in main.** `vellum:companion:contextMenu` handler builds `Size` submenu (radio over `COMPANION_SIZES`) + separator + `Hide Companion` (`companion-window.ts:756-792`). Labels from `packages/electron-desktop/src/companion-menu.ts:16-22`, shared with the tray's `Companion Size` submenu (`tray-model.ts:377-397`). `TrayModelRuntime.companionSize/setCompanionSize` is also implemented by the Windows stub (`clients/windows/src/main/tray.ts:59,69`).
- **Click-through is renderer-decided from ONE rect.** `companion-surface-page.tsx:290-318`: `within(pillRef)` || `within(introRef)` → `setInteractive`; `setHovered(onPill)`. Every comment in that file (`:157-167, :184-199, :206-227`) documents the prior bug where the window stayed interactive over empty canvas and ate desktop clicks.
- **Glow exists but is wrong in practice.** `companion-surface.tsx:914-920`: `size-10 animate-pulse blur-lg` with `background: accentHex`, gated to rest only (`:586`, `glow && !expanded`). The page derives `accentHex` ONLY from `call.accentHex` (`companion-surface-page.tsx:347-350`), so outside a call it is always the teal fallback `#5eead4` (`:115`), even though `character.color` is already in state. `animate-pulse` is n

payload.body: JARVIS-1631

payload.author: awlevin
payload.body:
Pushed two commits (`4297f0ea16`, `bc7fe41d37`) plus one open question for you, @awlevin.

## The schema default alone reached almost nobody

The default only governs an entry that omits `defaultRiskLevel`, and nothing wrote such an entry:

- `assistant/src/cli/commands/mcp.help.ts` gave `-r, --risk` a commander `defaultValue: "high"`, so the CLI sent `risk: "high"` on every `mcp add` whether or not the user passed the flag.
- `handleMcpAdd` then substituted `"high"` of its own for a body that named no risk, and persisted it.
- `handleMcpList` displayed `?? "high"` for an entry with no field, so the list would have misreported the level even once the default changed.

So every server ever added through `mcp add` (which is what `skills/mcp-setup` drives) carries a literal `"high"` in `config.json`. Changing the schema default would have moved only hand-edited entries.

Fixed in `4297f0ea16`: the flag has no default, the route persists `defaultRiskLevel` only when the caller names one, and the display falls back to the shipped default. `DEFAULT_MCP_RISK_LEVEL` in `config/schemas/mcp.ts` is now the one place the level is written down. Tests: `runtime/routes/__tests__/mcp-add-default-risk.test.ts` (new, asserts the written entry omits the field and parses to `medium`) and two updated cases in `__tests__/mcp-cli.test.ts`.

Also corrected the stale "default: high" text in the CLI help and `skills/mcp-setup/SKILL.md`, and regenerated `skills/catalog.json` (two of the three timestamp bumps were already stale on the branch).

## The question: this still does not fix the servers in the production table

The composio / plaud / lightpage installs behind those prompt rates already have `"defaultRiskLevel": "high"` sitting in their `config.json`, written by the old CLI default. On upgrade they keep it, so they keep prompting on every call, and `252fee2213` means `readOnlyHint` cannot help them either, since `high` is now the floor for downward hints.

That interacts with the safety argument in `252fee2213`: "a server sitting at high got there because the user put it there" is true going forward, but it is false for every server added before this PR, where the CLI put it there. On existing installs the two changes compose into no change at all.

Nothing here distinguishes a user who chose `high` from a CLI that defaulted to it, so I did not write a migration to strip those entries. That is the design call I want from you before doing anything else:

1. Ship as is, and existing installs stay at high until the user changes the level by hand.
2. Add a workspace migration that removes `defaultRiskLevel: "high"` from entries, accepting that it also clears levels a user set deliberately.
3. Something narrower, e.g. migrate only entries that match the exact shape the old `mcp add` wrote.

I have not touched the agreed behavior (medium default, one-step annotation adjustment) and will not without your say-so.

Renames the Settings timezone picker label from "Closest city" to "Timezone" across the UI (en/es/ru i18n), the aria-label, and the vellum-client-capabilities SKILL.md. Adds offset-shaped query resolution (`parseOffsetQuery`) so typing "UTC-4", "gmt+5:30", or "-07:00" matches zones by resolved offset minutes rather than substring. Two fixes landed in response to review and Codex findings:

1. **Minute field > 59 fails closed** (my prior blocking finding): `offsetMatchToMinutes` returns `null` for minute 60-99, so "UTC+5:60" produces "No matches" instead of aliasing to UTC+6. Both callers handle null correctly — `parseOffsetQuery` propagates it (returns null), `buildMetadata` falls back to 0 (only called for real IANA zones, never has minute > 59).

2. **Bare UTC and GMT resolve to zero offset** (Codex P2): `parseOffsetQuery` short-circuits `query === "utc" || query === "gmt"` to return 0 before the signed regex runs. Without this, "GMT" fell to substring matching and returned every zone (every offset label starts with "GMT"), and "UTC" returned nothing on ICU builds that omit the literal UTC zone.

<summary>▸ Analysis (2 findings)</summary>

- **A.1 — Test coverage is thorough.** Six tests cover: keyboard commit race (no debounce window), narrow-query highlight tracking, query-clearing clears highlight, offset matching across spellings (UTC-7/gmt-7/-07:00, UTC+5:30/+5:30/utc+0530), bare UTC/GMT zero-offset filtering (Reykjavik in, Tokyo out), and malformed minute fields (UTC+5:60/UTC+12:60/-0:60 all "No matches"). The Colombo-over-Kolkata choice avoids ICU canonicalization drift. No gaps.
- **A.2 — catalog.json regenerated over merged main.** The `updatedAt` timestamp changes on three entries are auto-generated from the catalog refresh, not hand-edited. The "Check catalog.json is up to date" CI check passes at this HEAD. The SKILL.md text update (Closest city → Timezone, placeholder alignment) is consistent with the UI changes.

</details>

<summary>▸ Minor (non-blocking, optional)</summary>

- **M.1 — `?? 0` in buildMetadata is a dead path.** `offsetMatchToMinutes` can now return null, but `buildMetadata` only calls it with offset labels parsed from real IANA timezone strings (e.g. "GMT+5:30"), which never contain minute > 59. The `?? 0` fallback is harmless defensive code that can never fire. Not worth changing.

</details>

payload.body: Plan papertrail: Assistant avatars in the chooser # Assistant avatars in the chooser ## Overview Show each assistant's avatar (character SVG or uploaded image) on the chooser cards in `select-assistant-screen.tsx`, which today render generic Laptop/Cloud/Link2 glyphs. Three data paths, matched to what each row type can actually reach: (1) live per-row fetch through the platform proxy — valid **only** in pure cloud mode, because every other mode's gateway discards the `assistant_id` path segment and would silently serve the connected assistant's avatar for every row; (2) an Electron/dev-host bridge method that reads `/.vellum/workspace/data/avatar/` off disk for local lockfile rows (works even while the assistant is asleep); (3) a daemon→platform sync that pushes the derived PNG raster onto the platform `Assistant` record (companion plan: `vellum-assistant-platform/.private/plans/assistant-avatar-field.md`), so `listAssistants` carries an `avatar_url` that renders in every mode with zero daemon round-trips. Character avatars render as the real SVG wherever traits are available (bundled components ship with the web app — no network needed); synced thumbnails are static PNG. Paired rows have no safe pre-connect transport (the paired gateway token is a single global slot), so they are covered by two fallbacks: the platform-synced `avatar_url` looked up by assistant id (PR 10 — works for any paired assistant that has run `vellum login`), and an IndexedDB last-seen cache filled whenever a row's avatar is observed live (PR 11 — covers everything else after one connection). Cross-repo ordering: PRs 1–8 and 11 here are independent of the platform repo. PRs 9 and 10 require the platform plan's PRs merged **and** the automated `automated/sync-openapi-specs` PR merged into this repo (so `clients/web/src/generated/api` has `avatar_url`). PR 8 (daemon sync) is skew-safe to merge before the platform field exists — DRF `ModelSerializer` ignores unknown request fields, and the startup re-sync backfills once the platform deploys. ## PR 1: ChooserAvatarChip component ### Depends on None ### Branch chooser-avatars/pr-1-avatar-chip ### Title web: add ChooserAvatarChip for rendering assistant avatars in list rows ### Files - clients/web/src/components/avatar/chooser-avatar-chip.tsx (new) - clients/web/src/components/avatar/chooser-avatar-chip.test.tsx (new) - clients/web/src/i18n/locales/en/common.json - clients/web/src/i18n/locales/es/common.json ### Implementation steps 1. Create `ChooserAvatarChip` (function declaration, named export, props interface `ChooserAvatarChipProps`) with props: `traits: CharacterTraits | null`, `imageUrl: string | null`, `size?: number` (default 48), `fallback: ReactNode`, `className?: string`. It is purely presentational — no fetching. 2. Character branch (`traits` non-null): load components via `useBundledAvatarComponents()` (`clients/web/src/utils/use-bundled-avatar-components.ts` — module-cached ~48 kB lazy chunk, no network). While components are still loading, render the `fallback` (the chooser's 48px slot holds its own size, so no reflow — same reasoning as `assistant-avatar-tile.tsx:20-30`). Once loaded, render `AvatarRenderer` (`clients/web/src/components/avatar-renderer.tsx`) with `bodyShapeId/eyeStyleId/colorId` from traits and the given `size`. Follow the precedence resolution in `clients/web/src/utils/avatar-render.ts` (`resolveAvatarRender`) rather than reimplementing it if it fits. 3. Image branch (`imageUrl` non-null, `traits` null): render `` with `rounded-full object-cover` sized `size × size` (mirror `chat-avatar.tsx:156`), `alt` from i18n. 4. Both null: render `fallback` verbatim. 5. i18n: the component lives under `src/components/` → **`common`** namespace (`clients/web/src/i18n/namespaces.ts:14-19`). Add a key like `chooserAvatarChip.alt` to **both** `en/common.json` and `es/common.json` (a key missing from either locale fails `catalogs.test.

<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Companion avatar restyle — implementation plan</summary>

# Companion avatar restyle — implementation plan

Source: Jason's two mockups (2026-08-26). (1) The avatar floats free of the options pill, glowing in its own colour, with the pill ("Talk / Type / …") beside it. (2) The right-click menu grows two submenus, "Avatar size" and "Options size", each with the same five steps (Small / Medium / Large / Huge / Ridiculous), above "Hide Companion".
Asks: separate avatar from pill; independent avatar vs options size; glow derived from the avatar's colour; slow, slight vertical bob.

Risk: **Yellow** overall (contract + main-process geometry + renderer hit-testing all change; the click-through invariant is the thing to protect). PR1 is Green.

## Audit of the current state (2026-08-26, three read-only investigations)

- **One shape, not two.** `CompanionSurface` renders a single root pill (`clients/web/src/components/companion-surface.tsx:514-538`); the avatar is an in-flow child of the pill's only row (`:580-598`), Talk/Type are its siblings (`:607-632`). The pill chrome is an absolutely positioned `<span>` faded by opacity (`:545-555`) so nothing is visible around the avatar at rest.
- **One scale for everything.** Size is the 5-step enum `COMPANION_SIZES` / `COMPANION_SIZE_BOXES` (`packages/ipc-contract/src/types.ts:670-692`, small=44 … ridiculous=220). Main resolves it to one number, `CompanionSurfaceState.avatarBox` (`types.ts:846-854`, published at `clients/macos/src/main/companion-window.ts:286-301`), and the page applies it as ONE `transform: scale(avatarBox / 44)` wrapper (`companion-surface-page.tsx:380-387`). `CompanionSurface` has no size prop; it knows only 44.
- **Persistence is one key.** `companionSize` in the `window-state` electron-store (`packages/electron-desktop/src/window-state.ts:44-48, 128-133, 160-165`). Never crosses IPC as a name.
- **Geometry is derived from that one number**: `geometryFor(size)` (`companion-window.ts:158-179`) sets `avatarBox`, `maxPillWidth = 360 * scale`, `riseAbove = 290 * scale - avatarBox/2 + pad`, `dropBelow = COMPANION_NEAR_EDGE * scale`, canvas = fixed box sized to the largest state. `BASE_MAX_PILL_WIDTH = 360` (`:102`) and `BASE_MAX_CARD_HEIGHT = 290` (`:117`) are hand-mirrored from the renderer's `FALLBACK_WIDTHS` (`companion-surface.tsx:172-177`) / `CARD_WIDTH` / `TURNS_MAX_HEIGHT`.
- **`COMPANION_NEAR_EDGE` (= 22 + 24 = 46) is the cross-process invariant** (`types.ts:719-734`): main's `dropBelow` and the renderer's `anchor` (`companion-surface.tsx:479-482`) and the intro card (`companion-intro.tsx:191`) all derive from it. Drift = avatar drawn somewhere other than where main believes it is (JARVIS-1582, `companion-surface.test.tsx:251-266`).
- **Menu lives in main.** `vellum:companion:contextMenu` handler builds `Size` submenu (radio over `COMPANION_SIZES`) + separator + `Hide Companion` (`companion-window.ts:756-792`). Labels from `packages/electron-desktop/src/companion-menu.ts:16-22`, shared with the tray's `Companion Size` submenu (`tray-model.ts:377-397`). `TrayModelRuntime.companionSize/setCompanionSize` is also implemented by the Windows stub (`clients/windows/src/main/tray.ts:59,69`).
- **Click-through is renderer-decided from ONE rect.** `companion-surface-page.tsx:290-318`: `within(pillRef)` || `within(introRef)` → `setInteractive`; `setHovered(onPill)`. Every comment in that file (`:157-167, :184-199, :206-227`) documents the prior bug where the window stayed interactive over empty canvas and ate desktop clicks.
- **Glow exists but is wrong in practice.** `companion-surface.tsx:914-920`: `size-10 animate-pulse blur-lg` with `background: accentHex`, gated to rest only (`:586`, `glow && !expanded`). The page derives `accentHex` ONLY from `call.accentHex` (`companion-surface-page.tsx:347-350`), so outside a call it is always the teal fallback `#5eead4` (`:115`), even though `character.color` is already in state. `animate-pulse` is n

This is the right product direction, and the current HEAD correctly fixes the bot-raised privacy gap: platform identities equal to the auth store's email/username fallbacks now go unidentified, with focused regression coverage. The React/Electron-renderer path, local-device identity choice, sign-in/sign-out subscription, and per-flavor seam are otherwise coherent.

<details>
<summary>▸ Analysis (1 blocking finding)</summary>

- **Blocking, Capacitor native late-init lifecycle:** `installSentryUserSync()` stamps the current user once and then only reacts to `authStore.user` changes. When diagnostics is closed at boot, that first `Capacitor.setUser()` happens before `Capacitor.init()`. In the exact shipped `@sentry/capacitor` 4.1.0 source, initialization only wraps future scope `setUser` calls to forward them through `NATIVE.setUser`; it does not replay the scope's already-stored user. If consent later opens while the auth user stays unchanged, native initialization receives no identity, so native crash envelopes can continue reporting Users: 0 until another auth transition. Reapply the current identity after every successful client initialization (or otherwise make client activation an input to the identity sync) and pin the consent-off-at-boot → later-opt-in path with a regression test.

- The previous Devin/Codex PII finding at `d34f9d1a` is independently verified fixed by `39ae236a55`: email and username fallback identities fail closed to `null`, and the focused tests cover both shapes.
- Territory check: open PR #41519 overlaps only in Sentry initialization. Its behavioral addition is an independent `ignoreErrors` append; shared test-file edits are identical formatting, so there is no current semantic collision.
- Migration check: none detected.

</details>

**Merge status:** blocked on the Capacitor native identity reapplication lifecycle above. Exact-head CI is 12/12 terminal green, but green CI does not cover the late client-initialization transition.

*Vellum Constitution — Trust-seeking: impact telemetry earns trust only when its privacy boundary and cross-surface attribution are both true in the lifecycle users actually run.*

✦ **APPROVE**

**Value:** Users on web and macOS get ~1200 fewer false-error Sentry events per week — cancellation noise (TanStack query cancels, browser fetch aborts) is correctly classified as control flow, so Sentry alerts and #sentry-assistant-clients alerts represent real failures instead of routine cache invalidation and unmount noise.

**Linear follow-up:** LUM-2984 — this closes it.

This teaches both error-reporting seams that cancellation is control flow, not failure. A shared `isCancellationError()` predicate gates `captureError()`, and type-anchored `ignoreErrors` patterns close the same gap for Sentry's automatic `onunhandledrejection` path. The fourth commit (1aeb2506) consolidates five hand-rolled `instanceof DOMException` abort checks in `stt-api.ts` and `pair-device-client.ts` onto the same predicate — fixing a real WKWebView bug where three sites only checked `instanceof DOMException` and missed plain-object aborts (a cancellation surfaced to the user as an error for their own action).

<details>
<summary>▸ Analysis (3 findings)</summary>

- **A1 — predicate design (is-cancellation-error.ts):** Uses TanStack's own canonical `isCancelledError()` (instanceof) plus `.name === "AbortError"` for the DOMException case. The `.name` check is the right call over `instanceof DOMException` — iOS WKWebView surfaces fetch aborts as plain objects carrying the name but not `DOMException` instances, which is exactly the bug the 4th commit fixes at the inline sites. The test suite covers CancelledError variants, all four engine AbortError wordings, WKWebView plain objects, and negative cases (TimeoutError, TypeError, plain Error with abort-like message, null, string). Clean.

- **A2 — ignoreErrors anchoring (sentry-init.ts):** The patterns `/^AbortError:/` and `/^Error: CancelledError$/` are anchored on the exception *type* prefix, not the bare message. This is the fix for Codex's P2 at the first commit — a first-party `ApiError` carrying "The operation was aborted." has type `ApiError`, so the bare value never starts with `AbortError:` and stays reportable. The test suite explicitly asserts lookalike messages with non-abort types are NOT filtered. This is correct and well-tested.

- **A3 — captureError gating (capture-error.ts):** The cancellation check sits after the transient-network check and before the bestEffort daemon-transient check, mirroring the existing layering. No behavior change outside error reporting. The PR description's claim that no SSE/stream caller relies on `captureError` reporting a deliberate abort is consistent with the codebase — watchdogs report via `captureMessage`/breadcrumbs.

</details>

<details>
<summary>▸ Minor (non-blocking, optional)</summary>

- **M1 — test mock spreading:** The three suites that partial-mock `@tanstack/react-query` now spread the real module (`...actualReactQuery`) before overriding stubs. This is the right pattern — keeps future named exports resolvable. The comment explaining why is helpful.

</details>

**Merge status:** Ready. 12/12 CI checks SUCCESS at exact HEAD `1aeb2506`. Devin "No Issues Found" at first commit; Codex P2 (type-anchoring) addressed in 4f7909982e and verified at HEAD. Trust-expansion applies — the HEAD delta (4th commit) is a refactor adopting the already-reviewed predicate at inline sites, not new behavior. `mergeable_state: blocked` is the unresolved Codex thread, being resolved now.

payload.author: alex-nork
payload.body:
Addressed the Codex review. Two of three fixed in `d7ea3aa0bb`; the third I'm declining on product grounds, reasoning below.

**P1 — Wait for capture before sending the seed turn: fixed, and it was a real bug.**

Confirmed the path: `finishCaptureStartup` fails the session via `finishWithError` → `teardown()` on a bad capture result, and the seed had already gone out synchronously in the `ready` handler. The daemon persists it and runs a turn regardless, so a denied mic left an instruction the user never wrote sitting in a brand-new thread, next to a cancelled response, in a conversation where voice never became usable. Since the entire reason the seed is gated on an empty conversation is that it persists *permanently*, this was exactly the harm the gate exists to prevent.

The seed now rides behind the capture-startup await and is spent only when `captureRunning` confirms a mic came up. The ref deliberately outlives a spent attempt, so a denial doesn't swallow the greeting — the next start that reaches a live mic still takes it.

Two regression tests, both verified to fail against the previous ordering:
- `never greets into a session whose microphone failed` — no seed, session reports `failed`
- `greets on a retry after a first attempt lost its microphone`

**P1 — Remove change history from code comments: fixed.**

Fair catch against AGENTS.md "Comments describe the present; PRs describe the history." Rewrote the `voice-entry-greeting.ts` docblock (dropped "The fix is") and swept the rest: `"the pre-JARVIS-1649 behaviour"`, `"the silent room it had before"`, and the diff-oriented `"This is why the seed is consumed on ready rather than..."` are all gone. Kept the bare `JARVIS-1282` pointer in one comment, which matches the surrounding convention in this file.

**P2 — Apply the greeting seed to deep-link starts: declining, deliberately.**

The observation is factually correct — `bindFreshConversation` mints a blank draft every time, so it *is* structurally the blank-thread case. But seeding it is the wrong call here, for the reason the blank-thread gate exists in the first place.

Every deep-link entry mints a fresh conversation, so seeding that path means **every single Siri / Action Button / Live Activity launch greets, without exception**. That is precisely the "greet on every entry" behaviour we considered and rejected when scoping this: it gets old fast, and here it would also mean an accumulating trail of identical self-authored instructions across a pile of one-shot draft threads.

The intent differs too. Reaching for the Action Button or saying "talk to Vellum" is *already* an utterance — the user has stated what they want. Being answered with "what would you like to work on?" asks a question they just answered. A composer mic click is ambient by comparison: you're in a chat window with nothing particular queued up, which is the case the greeting is for.

Worth noting the surrounding code already treats these two entries as different in kind: `start-voice-request.ts` deliberately skips `prewarm()` there because those paths have no gesture to borrow.

Happy to revisit as its own ticket if we want greeting-on-every-hardware-entry, but it's a separate product decision rather than an oversight in this change.

payload.author: vex-assistant-bot
payload.body:
✦ **REQUEST_CHANGES**

**Value:** Users who wake up to repeated background-job failure notifications get one actionable, human-readable alert ("You're out of credits. Add credits in Settings → Billing to continue.") instead of degraded code-only copy ("model_provider: Agent turn failed (PROVIDER_BILLING)"), because the turn classifier's full classification now rides the failure signal to the notification renderer.

**Linear follow-up:** LUM-3464 (In Progress, Ashlee) — stays open per PR description for post-#41295 items.

This PR carries the turn failure classification (authored user message, category, connection/profile attribution) across the turn boundary, consolidates every background-failure emission onto one seam (`emitBackgroundFailureSignal`), and renders the authored message instead of reconstructing degraded text. The architecture is sound — classify once, carry as data, render from it — and the additive-carrier design means old stamped rows degrade gracefully. The dedupe scope hierarchy (connection > profile > recomputed fallback) is the correct conservative direction.

However, CI is red with two test failures caused by the PR's own API changes. These block merge.

<details>
<summary>▸ Analysis (3 findings)</summary>

**Finding 1 — BLOCKING: schedule-retry.test.ts:546,601 — dedupe key regression**

The scheduler changed from consuming `result.failureCode` to `result.turnFailure?.failureCode` (scheduler.ts ~line 1062: `failedTurn = result.turnFailure`). The existing test mock at schedule-retry.test.ts:19-22 provides `{ errorKind, failureCode }` but NOT `turnFailure`, so `failedTurn` is undefined, `carried?.failureCode` is undefined in `emitAlert`, and `emitBackgroundFailureSignal` receives no `failureCode`. The dedupe key falls back to `errorKind` ("model_provider") instead of the classified code ("PROVIDER_BILLING").

CI evidence:
```
Expected: /^activity-failed:cause:PROVIDER_BILLING:balanced:\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/
Received: "activity-failed:cause:model_provider:balanced:2026-08-26"
```

This test file was not modified in this PR. Fix: either update the mock to provide `turnFailure: { failureCode: ... }`, or have the scheduler fall back to `result.failureCode` when `result.turnFailure` is absent (the `RunBackgroundJobResult` still carries `failureCode` as a convenience projection).

**Finding 2 — BLOCKING: plugin-import-boundary-guard.test.ts:554 — new plugin→host import not in baseline**

`sweep-job.ts` (a plugin file at `assistant/src/plugins/defaults/memory/substrate/`) now imports `../../../../notifications/background-failure-signal.js` — a host-internal module not in the plugin import boundary baseline. The old import (`emit-signal.js`) was in the baseline; the new one is not.

CI evidence:
```
- memory: "../../../../notifications/background-failure-signal.js" (e.g. src/plugins/defaults/memory/substrate/sweep-job.ts)
```

Fix: either regenerate the baseline with `UPDATE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_BASELINE=1` and explain the new coupling in this PR, or restructure so the plugin doesn't import the new host module directly (e.g. have the sweep job's caller inject the emit function).

**Finding 3 — non-blocking: copy-composer.ts:375 — unbounded `failureSummary` in rendered body (Codex P2)**

The new `activity.failed` template renders `payload.failureSummary` verbatim with no length cap, whereas the old template truncated `errorMessage` at 200 chars. The classifier's authored messages ("You're out of credits...") are short by design, but the `classifyByMessage` default branch can set `userMessage` to the first exception line (unbounded). A long single-line error would produce an oversized stored and pushed notification. Recommend truncating `summary` before assigning to `body` — a 500-char cap is reasonable for authored prose.

</details>

**Merge status:** BLOCKED — CI Test job is FAILURE at HEAD `131ed683`. Two test failures (findings 1 and 2) must be fixed and CI re-run green before merge. `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`.

Bot sig

# Collapse pairing onto one artifact: the pairing link

## Context

Pairing a second machine or device to a self-hosted assistant currently exposes four
user-visible artifacts: a QR code, a pairing URL, a short web approval code
(`ABCD-EFGH`), and a base64 pairing bundle. Only two of those are real mechanisms.

- **QR = pairing URL.** `pair-device-client.ts` mints a challenge, approves it locally,
  and produces one string (`verificationUri` + `#device_code=…`). The QR is that string
  rendered as pixels — the "Pair a device" card already shows both.
- **The user code is the reverse direction** — the device mints and displays a code, the
  host approves out of band. Genuinely different and worth keeping.
- **The bundle is the odd one out.** It exists only because the desktop importer never
  learned the device-code flow. `connect-assistant-dialog.tsx` → `importPairedAssistantBundle`
  → `pairAssistant` needs `gatewayUrl` + `token` + `refreshToken` + `deviceId`, and every
  one of those is obtainable from a device-code exchange.

The result is the "Connect a Remote Assistant" dialog demanding a base64 blob that only
`vellum pair` can produce, while the host UI three clicks away is already handing out a
perfectly good pairing link.

**Outcome:** one artifact — the pairing link — accepted by every surface. The dialog also
accepts a bare assistant URL and falls back to the approval-code flow, so pairing never
requires touching the host UI at all. The bundle is deleted.

### The one real blocker, and how it's solved

`gateway/src/http/routes/remote-web-pairing-token.ts:113-120` delivers the refresh token as
an **HttpOnly cookie**; the response body carries only `accessToken`. Correct for a browser,
useless for a lockfile writer. The gateway already does body-delivered refresh a few files
over (`gateway/src/http/routes/pair.ts:401`, via `mintAndRecordDeviceBoundTokenPair`), so
the exchange route gains a device-bound branch.

This grants no new authority: holding an approved device code already confers full pairing
rights, so letting the holder choose body delivery adds nothing. The SPA never sends a
`deviceId`, so browser posture is unchanged.

### Design decisions already settled

- **Where the exchange runs:** in the trusted host (`packages/local-mode`), not the
  renderer. Avoids CORS, keeps the device code out of the IPC boundary, and lets the CLI
  share one implementation.
- **Secrets stay host-side:** the host holds pending pairings in an in-memory map keyed by
  an opaque handle. The renderer only ever sees `{ handle, userCode, expiresAt }`.
- **No version gate needed.** An older gateway ignores the unknown `deviceId`, returns no
  body `refreshToken`, and the importer records the pairing as `accessOnly` — the existing
  expiry-warning path in the dialog. Graceful degradation for free.

---

## PR 1 — Gateway: device-bound branch on the token exchange

`gateway/src/http/routes/remote-web-pairing-token.ts`

Accept optional `deviceId` (and `platform`) in the request body. When `deviceId` is present:

- mint via `mintAndRecordDeviceBoundTokenPair` (`gateway/src/auth/guardian-bootstrap.ts:716`)
  instead of `mintAndRecordBrowserTokenPair` — per-device revocable, and it lands in the
  same `Paired devices` list the browser pairings do
- return `refreshToken` / `refreshTokenExpiresAt` / `refreshAfter` in the body
- emit **no** `Set-Cookie`, and skip `remoteWebRefreshCookiePathForPublicBaseUrl` entirely

Validate `platform` against a small allowlist (`cli` / `desktop` / `ios` / `android`),
defaulting to `desktop` — the value renders in the paired-devices list.

Absent `deviceId`, behavior is byte-identical to today.

Extend `RemoteWebPairingTokenRequest` / `…ApprovedResponse` in
`packages/service-contracts/src/remote-web-pairing.ts`, keeping the refresh fields optional
so the browser response shape is unchanged.

payload.author: noanflaherty
payload.body:
Review focus, in risk order:

1. **Loopback split (security).** `isLoopbackPublicUrl` stays the wide predicate (it is only ever read to *refuse* an address); the new `isDnsIndependentLoopbackUrl` is the narrow one, read only where loopback *earns* a privilege. Today that is `isConfidentialRefreshUrl`, which is what lets a refresh token travel in plaintext. If a future guard grants something to loopback, it wants the narrow one.

2. **Paired-id derivation (data).** The nameless default id goes from `paired-<host>` to `paired-<host><path prefix>`. No-prefix addresses derive exactly the same id as before, so existing entries are untouched. A deployment that *does* have a prefix and was paired by an older build keeps its old `paired-<host>` entry and credential; a fresh nameless re-pair of it registers a second entry under the new id rather than updating the old one. That is the intended trade: an extra entry the user can remove beats silently overwriting a different assistant's token.

3. **New pairing reason.** `import-precheck` is classified non-retryable (a blind retry is refused identically), and the new `pairingSessionSurvives()` is the separate axis a caller should read before dropping a session. **The web side is not wired up yet:** `connect-assistant-dialog.tsx` still calls `releaseSession()` on any non-retryable failure, so a name collision still discards a session whose code is good. The fix is one condition there (skip `releaseSession()` when `pairingSessionSurvives(polled.reason)`), owned by whoever owns `clients/web`.

4. **CLI test restructure.** `connect-import.test.ts` no longer leans on a 0.01s cadence to stay fast; `Bun.sleep` is stubbed to record each wait and advance a frozen clock by it. The suite got faster (207ms -> 82ms) and the cadence and backoff are now asserted exactly instead of implied.

payload.body:
<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Android Install Referrer Attribution + Native Auth Attribution Transport</summary>

# Android Install Referrer Attribution + Native Auth Attribution Transport

## Overview

Native (iOS + Android) signups currently land with **no marketing attribution at all**: `startAuthFlow`'s native branch drops `options.attribution`, `NativeAuthPlugin` has no parameter for it, and the platform's `SocialAccountAdapter.save_user` reads attribution only from OAuth redirect state that the Capacitor flow never produces. This plan builds the missing transport (PRs 1, 3, 4, 6), then feeds it from the Play Install Referrer API so Android installs from tagged Play links (`&referrer=utm_source%3D…`) produce a populated `UserMarketingAttribution` row at signup (PRs 2, 5, 7).

**Cross-repo.** The Django half lives in `vellum-assistant-platform` — see `.private/plans/android-install-referrer-attribution.md` in that repo (2 PRs, both dependency-free). The two repos' PRs are independent of each other and can run fully in parallel; end-to-end behavior requires both sides merged.

**Out of scope (flagged, not planned):** tagging campaign links on the marketing site (`vellum-website` repo) — required for the feature to deliver real value, but no such links exist in this repo. iOS gains no new data source here; its share of this work is parity per `clients/AGENTS.md` ("keep their handling aligned") plus carrying URL-param attribution that a Universal Link into `/account/signup?utm_…` already supplies.

### Reference: the current gap, traced

1. `clients/web/src/runtime/native-auth.ts` — `startAuthFlow` accepts `ProviderRedirectOptions` (which includes `attribution`) but the native branch calls `startNativeLogin({ returnTo, loginHint, intent })`, dropping it. Only the web branch's `startProviderRedirect` forwards it.
2. `clients/android/app/src/main/java/ai/vellum/assistant/NativeAuthPlugin.java:58` — `startAuth` reads only `baseURL`, `loginHint`, `intent`, `postAuthDestination`.
3. `WorkOSAuth.providerTokenRequestBody` posts `{provider, process:"login", token:{client_id, access_token}}` to `/_allauth/app/v1/auth/provider/token` (built by `buildPlatformURL`, no query string).
4. Platform `django/app/auth/adapters.py:327` — `attribution = _social_state_dict(sociallogin, "marketing_attribution")` resolves `None`, which also flows into `schedule_meta_signup_event` and `schedule_ga4_signup_event`.

The `vellum_utm` cookie fallback cannot rescue this: the native WebView's cookie jar never loads the marketing site.

### Invariants to respect

- **Skew rule** (`clients/web/docs/CAPACITOR.md:186`): the shell is a `server.url` shell, so an arbitrarily old App Store / Play shell can run an arbitrarily new web bundle. Every bridge call degrades silently — `console.debug`, never `captureError`, no availability probe, resolve empty.
- **One coherent source** (`persist_attribution` in the platform middleware): a row "with any attribution signal is a coherent unit from one source and must not be spliced with a second source's fields." The web layer therefore picks URL params *or* the install referrer wholesale — never merges them.
- **First-touch** is preserved server-side: `persist_attribution` only backfills a completely empty row.

---

## PR 1: Add a pure `Attribution` helper for the Android shell

### Depends on
None

### Branch
install-referrer/pr-1-android-attribution-helper

### Title
feat(android): add a pure attribution allowlist + query helper

### Files
- `clients/android/app/src/main/java/ai/vellum/assistant/Attribution.java`
- `clients/android/app/src/test/java/ai/vellum/assistant/AttributionTest.java`

### Implementation steps
1. Create `Attribution.java` following the pure-helper pattern of `AndroidAppLink.java` and `VoiceDeepLink.java` — package-private `final class`, private constructor, static methods only, no Android framework imports (so it runs under `:app:testDevDebugUnitTest`). Use `java.net.URLDecoder` / `java.net.

✦ **REQUEST_CHANGES**

**Value:** People using email can manage it in the same Channels surface as every other connection, eliminating the Settings detour while preserving setup, release, and trust controls.

**Linear follow-up:** [LUM-3134](https://linear.app/vellum/issue/LUM-3134/add-email-to-channels-and-take-it-out-of-settings) directly calls for one canonical home: Channels, not Settings.

The domain move is otherwise coherent: email derives from the existing readiness probe, the Channels domain owns the setup surface and copy, Settings no longer renders it, the prior card nesting and trust-floor findings are fixed at this HEAD, and all 12 CI checks are green.

**Blocking finding:** `profile-card.tsx:524` now links to `/assistant/channels?setup=email&release=1`, but arrival is handled by two independent replace navigations. `AssistantChannelsList` calls `selectAdapter("email")`, whose absolute navigation in `use-channel-route-selection.ts` drops the query string, while `useSetupChannelParam` separately removes `setup` through a search-only navigation. Those mount effects do not construct one atomic `/assistant/channels/email?release=1` location; depending on which navigation wins, either the Email panel selection or `release=1` is lost. The release confirmation therefore still is not guaranteed to open from the locked-handle door this PR claims to repair. Preserve the non-setup intent through channel selection and add focused coverage for the combined `setup=email&release=1` arrival.

**Merge status:** blocked on preserving the release deep-link action at exact HEAD `3fad13b2b08f7092cab2478777483eef3876737a`.

*Vellum Constitution, Inviting: putting email beside every other channel makes the product easier to approach, but every existing doorway must still carry the guardian's intent all the way through.*

**Value:** People using email can manage it in the same Channels surface as every other connection, eliminating the Settings detour while preserving setup, release, and trust controls.
